title: Trump threatens to take out Iran in ‘one night’ if no deal before deadline
byline: US President Donald Trump has threatened to take out Iran ‘‘in one night’’ if it fails to make a deal before the deadline he set for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global energy route.

title: Showers expected in parts of the island today
byline: Showers or thundershowers will occur at several places in Northern, North-central, Central, Sabaragamuwa, Uva and Southern provinces after 1.00 p.m, today (07), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: President to announce economic relief package in Parliament today
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has granted approval for a new economic relief package introduced by the Government for groups affected by the Middle East crisis.

title: Netflix debuts new ‘Playground’ gaming app for kids
byline: Netflix doubled down on its gaming efforts on Monday, launching a new app called ‘‘Netflix Playground’’ that would feature games built around popular children’s characters such as Peppa Pig and Sesame Street.

title: Cabinet approves fuel subsidy for fishing vessels
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has granted approval to provide a fuel subsidy for fishing vessels, the Fisheries Ministry announced.

title: Artemis II moon mission breaks Apollo 13 record for distance from Earth
byline: The four astronauts of NASA’s Artemis II mission cruised on Monday to the deepest point in space reached by any human, following the tug of lunar gravitational force en route to a rare crewed flyby over the shadowed far side of the moon.

title: Two persons electrocuted to death in Polgahawela
byline: Two individuals have reportedly died after being electrocuted on a plot of land in the Bangalawatta area of Polgahawela.

title: UN expected to vote on watered-down Hormuz resolution on Tuesday
byline: The U.N. Security Council is expected to vote on Tuesday on a resolution to protect commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, but in significantly watered-down form after veto-wielding China opposed authorizing force, diplomats said.

title: Over 670 fatal road accidents reported so far this year - Sri Lanka Police
byline: According to Sri Lanka Police, there has been a systematic increase in the number of road accidents reported annually.

title: 23 organised drug traffickers identified, Public Security Minister says
byline: A total of 23 organised criminals involved in large-scale drug trafficking operations have been identified, Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala revealed.

title: Middle East war means ‘all roads’ lead to higher prices, slower growth, IMF chief says
byline: The war in the Middle East will lead to higher inflation and slower global growth, the head of the International Monetary Fund told Reuters on Monday, ahead of a forecast for the world economy planned by the global lender for next week.

title: Apple’s foldable iPhone faces engineering snags, potential shipment delays – report
byline: Apple has been encountering setbacks in the engineering test phase of its first foldable iPhone, which could lead to delays in its mass production and product shipment schedule, Nikkei Asia reported on Monday, citing sources.

title: Netanyahu claims Israel has destroyed Iran’s largest petrochemical plant
byline: Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed that Israel has destroyed the largest petrochemical plant in Iran.

title: Special bus and train services in place for Sinhala and Tamil New Year
byline: The Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) has planned special bus services to facilitate public transportation for people travelling to their hometowns for the Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

title: Global stocks struggle, oil jumps as Trump’s Iran deadline looms
byline: Global stocks wavered on Tuesday, while oil prices were perched near $110 per barrel as the prospect of escalation in the war in the Middle East and the looming deadline for a deal to be reached kept nervy investors on the sidelines.

title: Donald Trump praises Artemis astronauts: ‘You’ve made history’
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday (April 06) called and congratulated the Artemis astronauts circling the Moon for making ‘‘history,’‘ telling them they’ve ‘‘made all America really proud, incredibly proud."

title: Four Sri Lankans arrested at BIA for attempted smuggling of medicines worth Rs. 10M
byline: Four individuals, including a woman, have been arrested at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) for attempting to smuggle a consignment of medicines worth about Rs. 10 million into Sri Lanka.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Sabaragamuwa, Central provinces and in Kurunegala, Anuradhapura, Mannar, Vavuniya, and Mullaitivu districts.

title: No power cuts, only electricity breakdowns: Energy Minister clarifies
byline: Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody stated that the government has not implemented any power cuts despite the ongoing energy crisis, clarifying that the intermittent disruptions are solely due to electricity breakdowns.

title: Govt. allocates Rs. 15 bln to provide relief for electricity consumers using less than 90 units
byline: The government has decided to provide relief to electricity consumers who use less than 90 units, under the government’s proposed new economic relief package for groups affected by the Middle East crisis.

title: Special relief package: Diesel subsidy up to Rs. 100 per litre, Rs. 20 for petrol
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake arrived in Parliament today to present the government’s proposed new economic relief package for groups affected by the Middle East crisis.

title: Key bridge linking Saudi Arabia to the island of Bahrain closes over threats from Iranian attacks
byline: The King Fahd Causeway, a key bridge linking Saudi Arabia to the island kingdom of Bahrain, closed early Tuesday over threats from Iranian attacks.

title: President announces special relief package in Parliament
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake arrived in Parliament today to present the government’s proposed new economic relief package for groups affected by the Middle East crisis.

title: President arrives in Parliament to announce economic relief package
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake arrived in Parliament, a short while ago.

title: Sri Lanka CERT warns public of rising festive-season social media scams
byline: The Sri Lanka Computer Emergency Readiness Team (Sri Lanka CERT) today (07) has issued a public warning regarding a significant increase in online scams and financial fraud attempts circulating across social media platforms during the Sinhala and Tamil New Year festive season.

title: Don’t travel by train today, Israeli military warns people in Iran
byline: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) is warning people in Iran not to take the train today.

title: 80 arrested in special police operation at Dambulla Economic Centre
byline: A total of 80 individuals have been arrested in a special two-hour police operation conducted within the Dambulla Dedicated Economic Centre.

title: Chinese national arrested at BIA for attempting to smuggle cigarettes
byline: A Chinese national passenger who attempted to smuggle a consignment of cigarettes worth Rs. 550,000 into Sri Lanka through the ‘Green Channel’, which is designated for passengers with no items to declare at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA), was arrested by Customs officials at BIA in the early hours today (7).

title: Three people killed in shooting near Israeli consulate in Istanbul
byline: Three people were killed and two police officers were injured in a gunfire incident near the building housing the Israeli consulate in ⁠Istanbul on Tuesday, media reports said.

title: 30 Indian fishermen repatriated from Sri Lanka
byline: At least 30 Indian fishermen have been repatriated from Sri Lanka today (07), according to the Indian High Commission in Colombo.

title: 12-hour water cut announced for Pelanwatta and several areas
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced a 12-hour water cut for several areas in Pelanwatta due to the prevailing dry weather conditions.

title: Artemis II astronauts heading back to Earth after flying around the Moon
byline: Nasa’s Artemis II mission is on its way back to Earth after completing a historic fly-by of the far side of the Moon.

title: Ex-SLRC Chairman Sarath Kongahage arrested by Bribery Commission
byline: The former Chairman of the Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation (SLRC), Sarath Kongahage and the former Director General, Devapriya Abeysinghe have been arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC).

title: King Fahd Causeway, linking Saudi Arabia to Bahrain reopens after attack threats
byline: The King Fahd Causeway, a key bridge linking Saudi Arabia and the island of Bahrain, reopened Tuesday (April 7, 2026) morning after closing for hours over possible threats from Iran.

title: Mojtaba Khamenei being treated for ‘severe’ condition in Qom, unable to govern Iran — report
byline: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is unconscious and is being treated for a “severe” medical issue in the city of Qom, while he is unable to govern the country, according to an intelligence assessment cited by The Times.

title: Nuwara Eliya PS Chairman arrested by Bribery Commission
byline: The Chairman of the Nuwara Eliya Pradeshiya Sabha has been arrested by officers of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC).

title: Iran war jeopardizes U.S. global leadership, warns Italian minister
byline: The Iran war has put U.S. global leadership on the line, Italy’s Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said, expressing fear about the “madness” of nuclear escalation.

title: Iran warns fuel will be cut off ‘for years’ if Trump carries out threat
byline: Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard warned Tuesday it would “deprive the U.S and its allies of the region’s oil and gas for years” if U.S. President Donald Trump carries out his threat to attack power plants and bridges if the Strait of Hormuz doesn’t open.

title: Iran’s president says 14 million have volunteered to sacrifice their lives
byline: Facing a looming U.S. deadline, Iran’s president said Tuesday that 14 million Iranians, including himself, have volunteered to sacrifice their lives in the war.

title: Israeli military says it has hit another petrochemical complex in Iran
byline: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) says it has struck a third petrochemical complex in Iran.

title: CEB prepared to provide power for New Year festivities – Minister
byline: The Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) has made arrangements to supply electricity for Sinhala and Tamil New Year festivals and various celebrations taking place across the country this month, Minister Vijitha Herath announced.

title: Special transport plan launched for Sinhala and Tamil New Year period
byline: The National Transport Commission has implemented a special transport plan to facilitate passengers traveling to their hometowns for the upcoming Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

title: Several large explosions heard on Kharg Island hours before Trump deadline
byline: Kharg Island in Iran appears to have been attacked, hours before Trump’s ‘deadline’ for the country to reopen the Strait of Hormuz arrives, Iranian media is reporting.

title: US oil prices top $115 a barrel after reports Iran’s Kharg Island targeted with multiple strikes
byline: Stocks retreated and oil rose as the war in Iran continued to intensify and US President Donald Trump threatened more destruction.

title: LP gas prices increased in Sri Lanka due to global gas price surge – Minister Vijitha Herath
byline: Domestic gas prices have been raised in line with the recent surge in global gas prices, according to Minister Vijitha Herath.

title: Sarath Kongahage and Devapriya Abeysinghe remanded until April 17
byline: The former Chairman of the Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation (SLRC), Sarath Kongahage and the former Director General, Devapriya Abeysinghe who were arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC), have been remanded.

title: Parliament to debate Sri Lanka’s prevailing situation tomorrow
byline: An adjournment motion regarding the current situation in Sri Lanka, to be moved by the government is scheduled to be debated tomorrow in Parliament.

title: Wireless music festival cancelled after Kanye West blocked from UK
byline: Promoter Festival Republic has cancelled Wireless Festival after Kanye West, who was due to headline the event in July, was blocked from entering the UK.

title: Trump says ‘whole civilisation will die tonight’ if Iran fails to make deal
byline: US President Donald Trump has just posted on Truth Social, warning: “A whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again”.

title: Audit reveals irregularities in coal procurement for Lakvijaya Power Plant
byline: A special audit report has uncovered multiple irregularities in the coal procurement process carried out by the Lanka Coal Company for the Lakvijaya Power Plant for the 2025/2026 season.

title: Train service cancelled in Iranian city after Israeli threat
byline: The governor of Mashhad in Iran’s northeast has reportedly suspended all train services in the city until further notice.

title: First photo from far side of the moon released
byline: The White House released the first photo taken by the Artemis II crew of the far side of the Moon on Tuesday.

title: Protest staged over principal appointment at Nayakakanda Good Shepherd Balika M.V.
byline: A protest was staged today (07) in Wattala over the appointment of a new principal to the Good Shepherd Convent Balika M.V.in Nayakakanda, Wattala.

title: Dept. for Registration of Persons working to restore system; Limited one-day service to resume
byline: The Department for Registration of Persons says efforts are currently underway to restore its computer system to resume normal operations.

title: President chairs meeting to discuss release of lands held by security forces in Northern Province
byline: The Ministerial Consultative Committee on Defence met in Parliament this afternoon (07) under the chairmanship of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, in his capacity as Minister of Defence.

title: Iran war could “spiral out of control,” Qatari official says
byline: Qatar warned on Tuesday that the region is close to a point where the situation could “spiral out of control.”

title: Indian tourist arrivals top 150,000 in 2026
byline: More than 150,000 Indian nationals have visited Sri Lanka thus far in 2026, data from the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) shows.

title: Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel struck railways, bridges in Iran
byline: Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel struck on Tuesday railways and bridges in Iran “used by the Revolutionary Guards”, after Iranian officials reported damage to at least two bridges and railway infrastructure.

title: Iranians begin forming human chains around power plants ahead of Trump’s deadline
byline: Iranians have gathered in large numbers at bridges and power generation stations across the country, forming human chains to prevent them from being targeted, the country’s state media reported on Tuesday.

title: Fuel bowser overturns on Badulla–Colombo road
byline: A fuel bowser overturned on the Badulla–Colombo main road at Puwakgahawela this afternoon (April 7).
